source_snapshot.procedure: Run fio on all drives with time_based, runtime=43200, bs=4K, rw=randrw, numjobs=32 depending on CPU design, size=4g, and iodepth=32.
source_snapshot.criteria: The system remains workable, system logs have no errors, and IOPS is at least 80% of the theoretical specification value.
source_snapshot.deepseek_finding: Only probe `fio --version` using an insecure SSH wrapper and return an unspecified result; it does not run the source workload.

original_test_intent.purpose: Run a 12-hour 4-KiB random mixed read/write reliability workload on every explicitly approved M.2 test drive, verify sustained storage performance against an approved reference, and confirm system/device health after the run.
original_test_intent.target: Each stable, owner-approved M.2 device/namespace or approved file target on the SUT; boot, OS, evidence, recovery, and unapproved data devices must be excluded.
original_test_intent.scope: A separately attributable result for every approved drive using time_based, runtime 43200 seconds, 4-KiB randrw, 32 jobs subject to CPU-owner confirmation, size 4 GiB, and iodepth 32 subject to precise per-job/target semantics.
original_test_intent.operation: Resolve a destructive-safe target/job matrix, preserve baselines, run tracked fio jobs for 12 hours with monitoring and complete output, then verify device/host health, data boundary, and performance per drive.
original_test_intent.duration_and_iterations: 43200 seconds (12 hours) per approved drive/job group. Simultaneous versus sequential drives, one versus 32 cloned jobs, and the meaning of 4 GiB for each clone/filename are not defined.
original_test_intent.expected_result: Every approved drive completes the full workload with no fio/media/controller/filesystem/kernel/BMC error, the host remains workable, and the defined per-drive IOPS metric is at least 80% of its comparable reference.
original_test_intent.required_evidence: Signed target/data-loss matrix, stable IDs and topology, fio version/job file, exact per-drive job semantics, 12-hour timestamps, complete JSON output including read/write IOPS/BW/latency/errors, device health/temperature/endurance deltas, host logs, cleanup/data-integrity status, and 80% calculation.
ambiguities: `all drives` does not exclude boot/OS/data/evidence devices or say sequential versus simultaneous.
`randrw` ratio, ioengine, direct/buffered mode, filename/namespace, cache/flush, verification, group reporting, ramp/measurement window, and CPU/NUMA binding are absent.
With numjobs=32, fio clones the job; `size=4g` is per thread/job and target/file semantics materially change the address range and data risk.
The theoretical value, metric units, read/write split, tolerance and aggregation window are not supplied.

v2_review_conclusion.finding: V2 correctly rejects DeepSeek's version-only probe, recognizes destructive all-drive risk, preserves 12 hours/4K/32 jobs/depth, requires stable non-system targets, read/write mix, baseline, monitoring, recovery, JSON and approval. It does not make the per-clone `size=4g` semantics or simultaneous-versus-sequential all-drive scope explicit enough for an execution agent.

applicable_history.decision: Destructive storage activity requires exact stable targets, impact boundary, backup/recovery, parameters, approval, full evidence, and stop conditions; high risk is not permanent non-automability.

v3_review_conclusion.summary: The 12-hour job is technically automatable only after a per-drive target/data-loss/profile matrix is approved. V3 preserves every fixed source parameter but requires explicit fio clone/file semantics, drive scheduling and a comparable per-drive 80%-of-reference calculation before any write-capable command is generated.

available_now: The M.2 context, 12-hour duration, 4-KiB mixed-random pattern, requested 32 jobs/depth 32/4-GiB region and health/performance objectives are explicit.
Read-only drive enumeration, stable identifiers, boot/mount/data classification, capacity/health/endurance/temperature, topology, workload and log baselines can be collected before write approval.
missing_inputs: Explicit allowlisted stable target for every drive, OS/data/evidence exclusions, raw-device versus file mode, accepted data-loss boundary, backup/restore and cleanup
fio version, job clone/filename/offset semantics, simultaneous/sequential drive schedule, rw mix, ioengine, direct/cache/flush/verify/grouping, CPU/NUMA policy, ramp and measurement/aggregation
Rationale/approval for numjobs=32 per target and confirmation of whether size=4 GiB applies to each clone, a shared region, or disjoint regions
Per-drive model/firmware/spec reference, exact read/write IOPS metric and 80% formula, temperature/endurance/error/latency abort limits, isolated window and recovery owner
execution_readiness_detail.input_owner: Storage/performance owners approve device mapping, fio profile, data boundary and reference; system/lab owners approve the maintenance window, backup/recovery, monitoring, limits and any package installation.
safe_read_only_work_before_closure: Enumerate NVMe/M.2 devices by stable ID and PCIe path; map boot/root/mounts/RAID/filesystems and evidence/recovery devices; capture controller/device firmware, SMART/NVMe health, endurance, temperature and errors
Record CPU/NUMA/controller topology, fio availability/version, free evidence capacity, active I/O, kernel/storage/BMC baselines and OOB access without clearing logs or opening targets for write
prohibited_until_closed: Do not autodetect `all drives`, address `/dev/nvme*` by enumeration order, include boot/data/evidence devices, install/run fio, create files, mount/unmount, or write any target before signed target/data-loss approval

Do not assume the default 50/50 randrw mix, silently choose ioengine/direct/cache semantics, multiply or share 4 GiB across clones by guess, shorten 43200 seconds, or use a version probe as completion
execution_readiness_detail.closure_verification: A generated dry-run manifest resolves each stable target and shows exact per-clone address/file range, total footprint, concurrency and output path; two-person target review confirms exclusions, the profile/reference/limits are signed, and abort/OOB/restore paths are tested without I/O.

revision_candidate.test_name: Twelve-Hour M.2 fio Reliability and Performance Validation
revision_candidate.purpose: Run the approved 12-hour 4-KiB random mixed read/write fio profile on every allowlisted M.2 test target and verify per-drive performance, device health, system stability, and data-boundary compliance.
revision_candidate.applicable_platform_environment: Dedicated server SUT with owner-approved M.2 devices, stable target mapping, pinned fio, protected evidence/recovery storage, adequate cooling/power, maintenance isolation, and OOB access.
revision_candidate.target_scope: Only allowlisted stable device/namespace or file targets in the signed matrix. Explicitly exclude boot/OS, user data, RAID members unless intended, mounted production filesystems, evidence destinations, and recovery media.
revision_candidate.required_inputs: Target/data-loss/backup matrix; fio version/job; exact rw mix, ioengine, direct/cache/flush/verify, clone/file/offset and grouping semantics; 32-job CPU rationale; depth/size/concurrency/schedule; 12-hour window; per-drive reference/80% formula; limits; monitoring; and recovery owners.
revision_candidate.test_command_procedure_intent: Generate one reviewed job section per stable target preserving `time_based`, `runtime=43200`, `bs=4K`, `rw=randrw`, approved `numjobs=32`, `size=4g`, and `iodepth=32`; add only owner-approved missing semantics. Validate target/range manifest before write, run tracked jobs in the approved simultaneous or sequential schedule, write full JSON and telemetry to a non-target evidence device, and collect per-drive results.
revision_candidate.preconditions: Two-person verified targets and exclusions, accepted data-loss boundary/backups, healthy devices, pinned fio/profile, no conflicting I/O, sufficient capacity/endurance/cooling/power, preserved logs, protected evidence destination, approved thresholds, and tested stop/OOB/recovery.
revision_candidate.expected_evidence: Approval matrix; stable IDs/models/firmware/topology; pre/post mounts and health; exact fio job/version; clone/range/footprint manifest; full 43200-second JSON/timestamps; read/write IOPS/BW/latency/errors per drive; health/temperature/endurance and kernel/BMC deltas; process cleanup; data integrity/restore; and auditable 80% comparison.
revision_candidate.acceptance_reference: Owner-provided per-drive comparable IOPS reference for the exact 4-KiB mix, queue/job concurrency, device count/schedule and system profile, with units, measurement window, aggregation and threshold `actual >= 0.80 × reference`.
revision_candidate.safety_restrictions: Write only signed targets/ranges. Never clear logs, use unstable device names, include boot/data/evidence media, guess fio defaults, overrun approved endurance/thermal/latency/error limits, auto-repair, auto-reboot, or auto-rerun after a storage fault.
revision_candidate.human_approval_requirements: Explicit approval is required for every target and data-loss boundary, exact fio job/concurrency, package, 12-hour window, performance reference, abort thresholds and recovery/restore plan.
revision_candidate.manual_boundaries: Owners identify and approve targets/data policy/reference; after immutable job approval, execution, monitoring, JSON capture, calculations and orderly stop are automatable. Fault recovery and final data-integrity judgment remain manual.
revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: Stop tracked fio PIDs, preserve partial output and logs, prevent automatic rerun, verify no job remains, collect health/mount/capacity state, execute only the approved restore/cleanup, and quarantine devices on media/filesystem/controller/data-integrity errors.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: Target identity or range mismatch, boot/data/evidence overlap, missing backup/recovery, unsafe baseline, active workload, allocation/capacity issue, media/NVMe/SMART/controller/filesystem/kernel error, data corruption, temperature/endurance/power/latency limit, monitoring loss, evidence-device risk, or incomplete job/output.

identified_defects: DeepSeek performs only `fio --version` and therefore does not execute any source workload.
The source's all-drive write scope lacks stable targets and a data-loss boundary.
The source omits fio semantics that control cache behavior, clone address/file ranges and mixed-I/O ratio.
The 80%-of-theoretical criterion is not comparable until metric, workload profile, per-drive reference and aggregation are defined.
reason_for_change: Make the write boundary and fio job expansion reviewable before execution so fixed source parameters cannot be turned into a guessed or cross-device destructive command.

new_technical_evidence.title: fio HOWTO
new_technical_evidence.applicability: fio job semantics; installed version must be verified
new_technical_evidence.supports: `time_based` repeats the workload until runtime; runtime without a unit is seconds; `numjobs` creates independent clones; `size` is the total I/O region per job/thread; randrw defaults to a 50% read mix if no mix is set.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: The testcase owner has not approved clone filenames/offsets, target mode, mix, ioengine or whether the source intended fio defaults.

removed_ambiguities: Separates 12-hour runtime from 4-GiB address region and from 32 cloned jobs.
Requires per-drive, not pooled, traceability and explicitly protects the evidence destination.
Defines the 80% comparison formula while leaving the missing reference to the owner.
resolved_blockers: fio package, target list and reference are supplyable conditions; read-only inventory can proceed before they are complete.
remaining_blockers: No write-capable job may run until targets/ranges/data policy, exact fio semantics, concurrency, baseline, thresholds, approval and recovery are resolved.
objective_improvement_over_v2: V3 retains V2's critical-risk and approval boundary but adds the official per-clone size semantics, all-drive schedule and evidence-device exclusion needed to prevent a guessed 32-job jobfile from overwriting the wrong data or producing untraceable pooled results.

per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_purpose_fact: The source requests 43200-second 4-KiB randrw on all drives with 32 jobs, iodepth 32 and size 4g, then compares IOPS with 80% of an unspecified value.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_v2_comparison: V2 catches destructive target risk; V3 makes clone-size/address, drive scheduling and protected evidence storage explicit.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_safety_evidence_decision: Generate no fio write command until stable targets and exact ranges are two-person approved; preserve 12-hour JSON, per-drive health and recoverability without clearing logs.
